source.title: Bias of Stochastic Gradient Descent or the Architecture: Disentangling the Effects of Overparameterization of Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Whole paper text present, including appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains randomly initialized networks to zero training error and studies how initialization, width, and depth affect outcomes, but its principal measures are generalization and normalized margin rather than the claim versions' training-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that SGD and G&C networks are selected or sampled to achieve zero training error. These are setup requirements, not results about whether training reaches near-zero error; the paper does not compare training error across depth, width, or initialization. Its results concern test accuracy, normalized loss/margin, and the probability of sampling a fitting network. Cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 3.3 reports that SGD attains zero training error for almost every random initialization in the study's strongly overparameterized, low-sample setting. This qualitative success-frequency result bears on V1, independently of the filtering of retained networks. The main generalization and margin results do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate, but SGD generalization stagnates or worsens with increasing depth rather than uniformly worsening. In low-sample binary MNIST and CIFAR-10 tasks, width improves SGD generalization while random fitting networks improve little; the authors attribute this difference to SGD's implicit bias. Depth worsens random-network generalization and stagnates or worsens SGD generalization, which they attribute mainly to architectural bias.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD with cross-entropy, fixed learning rate, batch size 2, and 60 epochs, alongside random Guess and Check sampling; filters or accepts networks that achieve zero training error. Studies binary low-sample MNIST and CIFAR-10 tasks and reports generalization, not the training-error outcomes in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: SGD outcomes depend strongly on initialization scale; width and depth produce different generalization patterns. The paper also argues that the choice of normalized loss changes comparisons across architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing width improves SGD test accuracy and geometric margin, while fitting networks obtained by random sampling show little improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width improves generalization through an implicit bias of SGD among networks that already fit the training data.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing depth worsens randomly sampled networks' generalization; SGD generalization stagnates or worsens. Random sampling also becomes less likely to produce a fitting network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth changes generalization and the probability of randomly sampling a fitting network in low-sample classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization changes final test accuracy and normalized margins; Uniform[-1,1] produces small gradients after fitting, whereas Kaiming or smaller-scale initialization permits continued optimization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization affects post-fitting margin optimization and generalization, even among networks with zero classification error.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: Experiments are restricted to binary classification and low-sample MNIST/CIFAR-10 settings; the paper avoids augmentation, weight decay, and sophisticated learning-rate schedules. Many reported trends are shown in figures, and the paper notes G&C's sampling cost grows exponentially.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: results report generalization, normalized loss/margin, and G&C fitting probability, while the requested versions concern training-error outcomes or other specific training behaviors. Figure results were therefore not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Full ten-class CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and systematic training-error comparisons involving model size, early stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, matched plain versus residual comparisons, and the special initialization recipes.
Initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth. Gradient norms, normalized margins and final test accuracy do not establish these outcomes.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult dynamics, curvature evolution and edge-of-stability training.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

missing.what: The qualitative SGD fitting-success result: zero training error is attained for almost every random initialization. Distinguish this report from the selection criterion that retained networks must fit perfectly; exact failure counts are unavailable.

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket exclusion of fitting outcomes overlooks the explicit almost-every-initialization result in Section 3.3. Retained models' 100% training accuracy alone would be a selection value and would not establish training success frequency. Generalization degradation with depth does not establish V3's training-error degradation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether sufficiently large convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam reach zero or near-zero classification error across CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted labels, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiments or measurements of spurious local minima by student/teacher width.
Does not measure training error as depth increases, compare plain and residual networks for training error, or test the cited special-initialization and normalization-free recipes.
Initialization is varied to study generalization, but the paper does not measure initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth as named in this version.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss-rise/curvature-drop, or sharpness-at-stability experiment.
No batch-normalization comparison or measure of accuracy gain speed or learning-rate tolerance.

relationships.condition: Strongly overparameterized networks on low-sample binary MNIST and CIFAR-10 tasks, using randomly initialized SGD for 60 epochs.
relationships.reason: Section 3.3 explicitly reports zero training error for almost every initialization; this supports fitting in the tested setting. Based on text because no row records this result; no exact success rate or architecture breakdown is supplied.
relationships.display_finding: SGD reached zero training error after 60 epochs from almost every random initialization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
